content.title: Community Engagement
content.summary: Arvada's city government is launching a comprehensive community engagement plan to shape the city's future, inviting input from all residents, including those who may not typically participate. The engagement process will unfold in four phases from 2026 to 2027, focusing on understanding the community's history, current conditions, future aspirations, and implementation strategies, with various opportunities for public involvement through meetings, surveys, and local events. The initiative aims to create a shared vision that reflects the diverse perspectives and needs of the community.
content.body:
![People talking at various tables](/ImageRepository/Document?documentID=7734 "People talking at various tables")

Your voice will be key to creating this shared vision for Arvada's future! We are developing a plan for engagement that will be as comprehensive as the Comprehensive Plan itself. Read on for an overview of how we'll be bringing you into the conversation.

---

## Our commitment

This is an opportunity to create a plan that you can see yourself in, incorporating feedback from highly engaged residents and other groups who don't join the conversation as often.

Our community engagement efforts will be:

### Collaborative

This is a team effort. As City staff and consultants, we will bring technical expertise and passion to this project. We invite you to share your preferences and unique insights as we balance needs and priorities to shape a plan we can all be proud of.

### Open and curious

We are here to listen to your experiences, your hopes, your dreams, your priorities. This plan will be shaped by the conversations we have together.

### Inclusive of all

Whether you are a long-time resident or new to the neighborhood, an HOA leader, a business owner or an employee, a student or an older adult, if you care about Arvada, we want to hear from you!

### Robust and trusted

A variety of tools and opportunities will be used to collect input from everyone who wants to weigh in, regardless of how much time they have. Whether you prefer to speak up at a public meeting, have a one-on-one conversation, or take an online survey, you’ll find a way to share your thoughts.

## Engagement timeline

![Timeline showing Phase 1 3-7 2026; Phase 2 8-11 2026; Phase 3 12 2026-4 2027; Phase 4 5-10 2027](/ImageRepository/Document?documentID=7489 "Timeline showing Phase 1 3-7 2026; Phase 2 8-11 2026; Phase 3 12 2026-4 2027; Phase 4 5-10 2027")

### Current status

Right now we are just getting started, meeting with our consulting team and putting plans in place for managing this project and how and when we will connect with you to provide ideas and input. We're currently in Phase 1 (see below).

### Phase 1: How did we get here?

**Timeframe**: Spring and Summer 2026  
**Purpose**: Understanding the community’s evolution and context.

**Key engagements**:

- Focus group conversations
- Interviews with community leaders
- Pop-up engagement at local events (e.g., AHS Community Night, Kite Festival, Summerfest)
- Community group connections
- High School Engagement Day at City Hall
- City Council and Planning Commission work session

### Phase 2: Who are we now?

**Timeframe**: Summer-Fall 2026  
**Purpose**: Assessing current conditions, challenges, and opportunities

**Key engagements**:

- Community listening and learning tour
- Pop-up engagement at local events (e.g., Arvada Days, Trick or Treat Street)
- Community Advisory Group (CAG) convened
- City Council update

### Phase 3: Where do we want to go?

**Timeframe**: Winter-Summer 2027  
**Purpose**: Establish a shared vision (guiding principles) and test drive future options (scenario planning)

**Key engagements**:

- Pop-up engagement at local events (e.g., Winterfest, Touch-a-Truck, Kite Festival)
- Community group connections
- Scenario Choosing community meeting
- Community Advisory Group (CAG) continues meeting
- City Council update

### Phase 4: How do we get there?

**Timeframe**: Spring-Fall 2027  
**Purpose**: Translating the preferred direction into policies, maps, and implementation strategies

**Key engagements**:

- Pop-up engagement at local events (e.g., Winterfest, Touch-a-Truck, Kite Festival)
- Public open house
- Community group conversations
- City Council study session
- Planning Commission and City Council public hearings

## Key event recaps

### Group of high school students file past a table of smiling staffArvada High School and Arvada West High School Engagement Event

March 4, 2026

Students from two area high schools — Arvada High School and Arvada West High School — came to City Hall for a day of workshops, tours, and conversation with City leaders.

**What you told us**

- Pedestrian and transit improvements are needed, including widening sidewalks and more accessible bus stops
- Increased density and variety of more affordable housing types would help young people see themselves staying in Arvada in the long term
- Greenhouse gas reduction and water conservation are of high importance to young people

**What we did with your feedback**

The feedback we received was invaluable at this stage in the project. Each of the key themes will be taken into account as we plan future engagements to shape and refine the Plan.

## Stay in touch

What's missing from this page? Is there a group you'd really like us to work with? Do you have a great idea for an event or engagement opportunity? Let us know! Send an email to the Comp Plan team at [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#c9aaa6a4b996b9a5a8a789a8bbbfa8ada8e7a6bbae). We also encourage you to [sign up for our bimonthly newsletter](https://app.e2ma.net/app2/audience/signup/2101013/1717219/) to stay up-to-date on the Comprehensive Plan project.
